ai.description: This 45–60 mm frog is green above with a white belly and distinct orange-red webbing between its fingers and toes. It features a pointed snout and a prominent white ridge along the outer forearm.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Zhangixalus suffry* is best distinguished by the vibrant, uniform reddish-orange webbing between its fingers and toes, which lacks the dark spotting found in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Zhangixalus suffry* inhabits subtropical evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Suffry red-webbed treefrog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for insects among the dense vegetation of its humid forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Zhangixalus suffry* breeds during the monsoon, depositing foam nests on vegetation overhanging water bodies. Each clutch contains approximately 100–150 eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Suffry Red-webbed Treefrog is found in the evergreen forests of Northeast India, specifically within Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, at elevations of 200–1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Zhangixalus suffry* consists of a series of short, high-pitched "tuck" notes, typically heard from vegetation near forest pools or streams.
